scenarios.name: normal_delta_t
scenarios.description: A heating loop doing its job: 70 degC supply, 58 degC return, pumps at 60%. The 12 K delta-T is above design, the rule is evaluated and silent.

scenarios.name: low_delta_t
scenarios.description: The fault: 70 degC supply, 66 degC return, pumps at 60%. A 4 K delta-T against a 5.5 K trip line, and the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay because delayOnInit holds the condition from the first tick. Return water this warm also costs a condensing boiler its condensing mode.

scenarios.name: quiet_loop_is_not_evaluated
scenarios.description: NO_EVAL: a 1 K delta-T with the pumps at 20%. Almost no water is moving, so almost no heat is being picked up and the delta-T says nothing about the distribution system. yLoadOk = false is what the host reads instead of a verdict.

scenarios.name: delta_t_exactly_at_the_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary, bit-exact: 65.5 - 60.0 is exactly 5.5, and 11.0 x 0.5 is the same double (both operands and the product have trailing zero mantissa bits, and halving is exact). Reals.Less is strict, so a loop sitting exactly on the trip line reads healthy.

scenarios.name: delta_t_just_below_the_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary from below: 65.49 - 60.0 clears the strict comparison by 10 mK and alarms on the normal schedule.

scenarios.name: delta_t_just_above_the_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary from above: 65.51 - 60.0 is above the trip line and never alarms, however marginal the loop's performance is.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_exactly_at_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: Boundary on the other conjunct: pump speed exactly at min_pump_speed_for_eval (35%) with a collapsed 4 K delta-T. Reals.GreaterThreshold is strict, so exactly-at-the-floor is NO_EVAL and the rule stays silent.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_just_below_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: 34.9% speed with the same collapsed delta-T: still NO_EVAL.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_just_above_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: 35.1% speed with the same collapsed delta-T: evaluable, and the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay. Two tenths of a percent of drive speed is the whole difference between this scenario and the one before last.

scenarios.name: delta_t_collapses_mid_run
scenarios.description: A loop running at a healthy 12 K delta-T loses it at t = 1800 s - a zone valve failing open, or a bypass opening as the building unloads. The alarm lands at exactly 5400 s: the mid-run rising edge carries the same T + delayTime arithmetic as the init case.

scenarios.name: delta_t_recovers_after_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 3600 s and the return temperature drops back at t = 5400 s. TrueDelay passes the falling edge with no delay, so yFault clears on that tick.

scenarios.name: pumps_slow_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The evaluability release: an alarming loop drops to 20% pump speed at t = 5400 s with the low delta-T unchanged. yFault and yLoadOk fall on the same tick, and only the pair tells the host that the loop went quiet rather than that the delta-T recovered.

scenarios.name: intermittent_low_delta_never_alarms
scenarios.description: Delta-T alternating between 4 K and 12 K every 1200 s - a hunting mixing valve, or zones opening and closing against each other. No single episode reaches alarm_delay, so nothing fires. Persistence is not averaging: a loop spending half its day at 4 K is a real finding this rule cannot make.

scenarios.name: supply_and_return_sensors_swapped
scenarios.description: Blind spot, pinned: the two temperature sensors are wired backwards (supply reads 60 degC, return 70 degC), so delta-T reads -10 K. Nothing in the graph knows a negative heating delta-T is impossible, and the rule reports the strongest possible low-delta-T fault on a loop that may be running perfectly.

scenarios.name: loop_circulating_with_no_heat_input
scenarios.description: The second blind spot, pinned: pumps at 70% around a loop the boilers are not heating, so supply and return equalise at 45 degC and delta-T reads 0.5 K. The rule alarms, and the finding is wrong - there is no distribution defect, there is no heat. This is the case operating_states excludes and HW-0003 detects.
